conflict_resolution.context: Resolves In-Memory Mutex Locking vs Database / Distributed Locking

opposing_principles.principle_a: In-memory synchronization (Mutex/Locks) is extremely fast, zero-latency, and trivial to mock in unit test harnesses.
opposing_principles.principle_b: Modern backend services are horizontally scaled and stateless. In-memory locks exist exclusively within a single process heap and are completely invisible across multi-pod load-balanced deployments.

verdict.rule_summary: In-memory promise mutexes are STRICTLY CONFINED to single-process test doubles (Mock/Fake repositories). Production services MUST enforce concurrency at the Database layer (SELECT FOR UPDATE) or Distributed Lock layer (Redis Redlock).

boundary_conditions.condition: An in-memory KeyedMutex (with identity-safe Promise tracking) may be used to serialize test executions.
Banned from using Node.js memory locks for shared state mutations. Must use PostgreSQL row locks or Redis distributed locks.
